title: Pantigo
summary: Pantigo names a locality between East Hampton village and Amagansett. The place is also associated with Pantigo Hill, where a seventeenth-century Montaukett cemetery was documented in the early twentieth century.
map_geometry_source: Public orientation point from OpenStreetMap/Nominatim for Pantigo hamlet; not a cemetery boundary or burial location.
history_content: East Hampton locality, Pantigo Hill landscape, Montaukett cemetery context, and later linguistic correction are brought together here. Town and archaeological details appear in the historic moments below.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Pantigo and Pantego. The history preserved here also records a correction to an older English-phrase explanation: later linguistic review interpreted Pantigo as an Algonquian name connected with a tidal inlet or a view of a tidal inlet.

Why Place Names Matter

“Local place names, often neglected in formal cartography, preserve cultural memory and linguistic identity while facilitating cross-cultural understanding.”

— Saltanat E. Davletova, Aigul Y. Bizhkenova, and Tatiana A. Burkova, Place, Memory, and Language: Vernacular Toponyms as Cognitive Anchors in Global Communication (2025), Abstract
whereintheworld_content: Map location note: near Pantigo Hill, between East Hampton village and Amagansett. The map marker orients readers and is not an exact cemetery boundary, burial location, or lot boundary.
